prospect.name: Jason
prospect.occupation: Self-employed — owns and runs a ranch training horses. Physically demanding, on and off horses all day. Former military. Controls his own schedule entirely.
prospect.family_status: Three boys aged 3, 12 and 14. The 12- and 14-year-olds race bicycles competitively; the 14-year-old is the one who found Trevor's content.
prospect.training_background: Effectively none — 'So zero. I say zero, but every now and again I'll be like, man, I'm feeling too fat, so I'll just knock out some push-ups or some burpees.' Was very fit and active in endurance sports as a young adult and served in the military. Has a small home gym built for his 14-year-old. Work provides constant incidental activity but no structured training.
prospect.medical: Self-describes accumulated wear — 'I know I have just some degenerative life in there'. Knee discomfort and stiffness kneeling or rising from the floor, rated 4-5 on his own scale, worse when tired; mobility self-rated 6-7 out of 10. Chronic lower back tightness and soreness he attributes to riding. No diagnosis, no clinician mentioned, and no medical assessment referenced.

signals: Was fit as a young adult and in the military and has lost it: 'My young life was very busy... I was a skinny kid, and I was very, very fit, very, very active in endurance sports'
Trigger is a recent realisation of decline rather than a crisis: 'I'm hitting some hurdles, and I'm noticing now for sure in the last few years that those random things are becoming harder'

Reads partly as the_preserver — 51, wants to hold function rather than gain, high nominal income with low liquidity at this point in the year — but he does want to gain (lean out, get stronger) and he is not medically managed, so rebuilder is the closer fit
Decline is measurable to him in work terms: 'I might have used to be able to move 50 bales, and after 15 bales, I got one of the boys to do it for me'

goals.text: Be strong and mobile enough to kneel, bend and get up without a twinge
Get stronger and stop the decline in work capacity
Lean out and lose the belly he carries all his weight in
Have plenty of energy and be able to move all day, any day
Still be able to whoop his boys and keep up with them at 80, and be there for the three-year-old in twenty years
Be a fit role model, particularly for the 14-year-old who is starting to lift
Keep doing the ranch work he loves for another thirty years without his body limiting it

pains.text: Knees signal stiffness and soreness when kneeling or getting up off the ground, and it is getting harder
Chronic lower back tightness and soreness from riding all day
Doing no structured training at all and knows it
Erratic snack-based eating — muffins, beef jerky, crackers, cheese, drive-through — because he eats on the move
Carries all his weight in his belly and dislikes it, and believes it is partly genetic
Will not walk into a gym — 'It's full of people. It's just not my jam'
Losing work capacity and delegating physical tasks to his employees
Two major shows over the next 45 days that are heavily cash-out-of-pocket

objections.raw_quote: I didn't intend to spend $6,000 in a lump. And so then I would have to determine a start date because of uniquely, actually, just because of my business, the things that I have over the next window of time, I'd have to determine, do I want to use that cash right now for this?
objections.rep_response: Isolated it properly — established it was timing rather than fear or value ('It's a timing piece from what I'm hearing, right? It's not like I don't want to do this, I'm scared to do this') — then improvised an instalment structure on the call.

objections.raw_quote: I didn't have any way of determining a number other than, yeah, I didn't really have a ballpark or even have a clue... That doesn't seem ridiculous to me, but at the same time, I have no idea what I was expecting, so I'd have to... process like, how do I do that or do I want to do it that way? But yeah, I mean, it's not scary.
objections.rep_response: Ran the 'if $6,000 fell on your lap' isolation and confirmed he would proceed, establishing value was not the issue.

tiers.note: Improvised instalment structure — 'six terms' at $1,200 each, i.e. $1,000 plus a $200 per-term surcharge, totalling $7,200. Not a listed tier.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Rep: 'We could do it in six terms, but it does then does add 200 per term, so that makes it 1,200 more. Maybe if we just start with the 1,200 rights, then we do it again next month if that's needed, and then after that we can just do the rest, and then the 200 goes away, basically.' No total was stated, no schedule was written down, and the conditions under which the $200 surcharge is removed were left ambiguous.

prospect_financials.note: Stated ceiling for an initial outlay was $1,000: 'I don't know that I'd want to be out of pocket more than about $1,000 to start.' Cited two major shows in the next 45 days that are heavily cash-out-of-pocket and a personal floor below which he will not let his balance fall.

evidence: Verbal agreement to the instalment structure was given: 'That seems much more intelligent to me, especially just the timing' and, to 'Let's just get started then?', the reply was 'Here, hold on one second, please.'
The call was then interrupted by a family emergency — a child crying — and terminated before anything was sent, signed or paid.
No payment link was sent, so the verbal_agreement_plus_link_sent rule does not apply.
A continuation call was booked for the same day at 2:30pm his time, invite sent and confirmed on the call: 'I've sent you an invite for 2.30 your time' → 'Okay.'
Rep stated the intent explicitly: 'what we would do now is we just go through everything, get you started. And then we also directly booked a meeting with Trevor.'

Counter-evidence on this being a genuine follow_up rather than a functional close: intent was very high, price was accepted, the structure was agreed and the gap was two and a half hours. The likeliest true disposition resolves in the 2:30 recording, which is not in this batch.
outcome.next_step: Continuation call the same day at 2:30pm CT to complete signup, take the first payment and book the onboarding call with Trevor.

notable.note: The most consequential pricing improvisation in the batch. The prospect said his ceiling for an initial outlay was $1,000; the rep proposed a first payment of $1,200 — above the stated ceiling — inside a six-term structure that totals $7,200, a $1,200 surcharge over the list price. The explanation given was garbled to the point that no total was ever stated and the conditions for removing the surcharge were never made clear, and the prospect agreed anyway. Separately: a 51-year-old who describes 'some degenerative life in there', knee pain kneeling and rising, and chronic low back soreness, doing zero structured training, was moved to purchase with no question about whether any clinician had assessed any of it.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained inversion. Long blocks of rep speech are attributed to 'Jason's iPad' — including the entire opening frame at 00:00:30 and most of the pillar presentation — and several of the prospect's own answers are attributed to the rep, including his height, weight and age at 00:07:02. Multiple turns are merged under a single label. Every attribution here was resolved from content.
